headline: Finnish Defence Minister Antti Hakkanen urges Europe and Indo-Pacific partners to unite on stronger Russia sanctions
dek: Hakkanen said Russia is deepening ties with China and North Korea, urged Japan-Europe cooperation on the grounds Europe/Indo-Pacific security is interconnected, and said economic penalties are essential to peace ('if Russia's economy suffers, Moscow will have no choice but to join peace talks').…
sources: Finnish Defence Minister Antti Hakkanen, NHK interview in Tokyo
fault_line: Sanctions as the lever that forces Moscow to talk -- or a lever Washington has already set aside ahead of November talks?

sections.what_happened: Hakkanen said Russia is deepening ties with China and North Korea, urged Japan-Europe cooperation on the grounds Europe/Indo-Pacific security is interconnected, and said economic penalties are essential to peace ('if Russia's economy suffers, Moscow will have no choice but to join peace talks'). He commented on the Trump administration exempting Russia from most sanctions in a recent US law and said countries must understand sanctions are essential. He pointed to the Oct 20 Norway meeting (Zelenskyy, Stubb, Witkoff) as efforts to get negotiations back on track, with discussion now on what is needed to initiate talks with Putin.
sections.what_verified: NHK only. NHK has NO declared tier in ~/workspace/times-dashboard/data/source-registry.md, so it contributes ZERO corroborating families under the registry rule.
sections.what_disputed: The US exemption itself is the counterweight: Washington in mid-October authorised Russian diesel transactions to Apr 7 2027 and extended Lukoil-related exceptions to Apr 24 2027, and Trump declined the Graham Act 'hell sanctions' (Riddle Russia analysis, mid-October) -- i.e. the sanctions-split Hakkanen complains about is an active US policy choice, not a misunderstanding. No new sanctions decision by Finland, the EU or Japan is reported in the interview.
sections.why_matters: Feeds the US-EU sanctions-split thesis (proven lane: NATO/Russia warnings); NOT a standalone Short -- rhetoric, no decision, single unregistered outlet.
